claim: CNBD ion channels are vital for cellular signaling and excitability, with activation regulated by cAMP or cGMP binding.
source: Cyclic nucleotide-binding domain (CNBD) ion channels are vital for cellular signaling and excitability, with activation regulated by cyclic adenosine- or guanosine-monophosphate (cAMP, cGMP) binding.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about CNBD ion channels.

claim: The allosteric mechanisms underlying CNBD channel activation remain unclear.
source: However, the allosteric mechanisms underlying this activation, particularly the energetics that describe conformational changes within individual domains and between domains, remain unclear.
evidence: This is an assertion about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The prokaryotic CNBD channel SthK has been a useful model for understanding allosteric mechanisms.
source: The prokaryotic CNBD channel SthK has been a useful model for better understanding these allosteric mechanisms.
evidence: This is supported by references to prior work on SthK throughout the manuscript.

claim: Time-resolved tmFRET was previously applied to investigate conformational dynamics and energetics in the CNBD of SthKCterm.
source: Previously, we applied time-resolved transition metal ion Förster resonance energy transfer (tmFRET) to investigate the conformational dynamics and energetics in the CNBD of a soluble C-terminal fragment of the SthK protein, SthKCterm (Eggan et al., 2024).
evidence: This refers to previously published work by the authors.

claim: The study used tmFRET to measure conformational energetics of the CNBD in full-length SthK channels.
source: Here, we used a similar strategy to measure the conformational energetics of the CNBD in the full-length channel, SthKFull, and compared them to measurements from SthKCterm.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the current study.

claim: The study incorporated the noncanonical amino acid Acd as a FRET donor and a metal bound to a chelator conjugated to a cysteine as an acceptor.
source: We incorporated the noncanonical amino acid Acd as a FRET donor and a metal bound to a chelator conjugated to a cysteine as an acceptor.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC) was used to measure time-resolved FRET.
source: We used time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC) to measure time-resolved FRET and fit the TCSPC data to obtain donor-acceptor distance distributions in the absence and presence of cAMP.
evidence: This describes the experimental technique used.

claim: The presence of SthK transmembrane domains makes the activating conformational change in the CNBD more favorable.
source: Our data indicate that the presence of the SthK transmembrane domains makes the activating conformational change in the CNBD more favorable.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: CNBD channels are activated when cyclic nucleotides bind to the CNBD of tetrameric channels.
source: CNBD ion channels are essential for a variety of physiological processes and are activated when cyclic nucleotides bind to the CNBD of these tetrameric channels (Craven and Zagotta, 2006; He et al., 2014; Matulef and Zagotta, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Upon ligand binding, CNBD channels undergo conformational changes resulting in the opening of the channel pore.
source: Upon ligand binding, CNBD channels undergo conformational changes resulting in the opening of the channel pore.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CNBD channel function.

claim: The channel pore is over 60 Å away from each of the four peripheral cyclic nucleotide binding sites.
source: However, this pore is over 60 Å away from each of the four peripheral cyclic nucleotide binding sites, and the allosteric mechanisms that underlie this 'activity at a distance' to open the pore remain incompletely understood (Evans et al., 2020; James and Zagotta, 2018; Craven et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a structural fact about CNBD channels supported by citations.

claim: The mechanism of ligand activation in SthK remains unclear from an energetic perspective despite substantial structural and functional information.
source: Yet, even with substantial structural and functional information of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) binding in SthK (Brams et al., 2014; Schmidpeter and Nimigean, 2021; Rheinberger et al., 2018; Schmidpeter et al., 2018; Marchesi et al., 2018), the mechanism of ligand activation remains unclear from an energetic perspective.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Previous work utilized time-resolved tmFRET to investigate conformational and energetic changes of the CNBD in SthKCterm.
source: Our previous work utilized time-resolved transition metal ion FRET (tmFRET) to investigate the conformational and energetic changes of the CNBD in an isolated C-terminal fragment of SthK (SthKCterm, Figure 1A, left) (Eggan et al., 2024).
evidence: This refers to previously published work by the authors.

claim: tmFRET uses the efficiency of energy transfer between a donor fluorophore and a light-absorbing metal ion acceptor to measure molecular distance.
source: tmFRET uses the efficiency of energy transfer between a donor fluorophore and a light-absorbing metal ion acceptor to measure the molecular distance between the donor and acceptor.
evidence: This describes the principle of the tmFRET technique.

claim: Distance distributions were obtained for the movement of the C-helix relative to the beta-roll of the CNBD in the presence and absence of ligand.
source: Distance distributions were obtained for the movement of the C-helix relative to the beta-roll of the CNBD in the presence and absence of ligand, which allowed for the calculation of the change in free energy (ΔG) and differences in free energy change (ΔΔG) induced by cyclic nucleotide.
evidence: This describes results from previous work.

claim: It remained unclear how the CNBD conformational change might look in the full-length channel and how the energetics might differ between the full channel and SthKCterm.
source: However, as these SthKCterm measurements were made in a truncated fragment of the protein, it remained unclear how the CNBD conformational change might look in the full-length channel (SthKFull, Figure 1A, right) and how the energetics of this transition might differ between the full channel and SthKCterm.
evidence: This identifies the knowledge gap addressed by the current study.

claim: A modular gating scheme provides a framework for integrating structural and energetic contributions across protein regions.
source: We approach this question using a modular gating scheme, also known as an ensemble allosteric model, which provides a framework for integrating structural and energetic contributions across protein regions, as illustrated in Figure 1B (Horrigan and Aldrich, 2002; Motlagh et al., 2014; Hilser et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the theoretical framework used, supported by citations.

claim: For SthK and related CNBD channels, the structural domains are defined as the pore, C-linker, and CNBDs.
source: In this model, allosteric transitions occur through coupled conformational changes in defined modules, which for SthK and related CNBD channels, we define as the structural domains of the pore, C-linker, and CNBDs (Figure 1A).
evidence: This defines the modular structure used in the analysis.

claim: Each module has a conformational equilibrium between its resting state and active state described by a corresponding free energy change, ΔG.
source: Each module has a conformational equilibrium between its resting state (R) and active state (A) (vertical arrows in Figure 1B) that is described by a corresponding free energy change, ΔG.
evidence: This describes the theoretical model used in the study.

claim: Transitions in individual modules are not independent but are coupled to each other.
source: Importantly, these transitions in individual modules are not independent but are coupled to each other (horizontal arrows in Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes a key feature of the modular gating model.

claim: Coupling is the amount by which the energetics of a module's transition is changed by the state of the neighboring module (ΔΔG).
source: Coupling is the amount by which the energetics of a module's transition is changed by the state of the neighboring module (ΔΔG).
evidence: This defines the concept of coupling in the modular gating model.

claim: Time-resolved tmFRET offers insights into protein conformational and energetic changes by using fluorescence lifetimes to quantify distance distributions.
source: Time-resolved tmFRET offers insights into protein conformational and energetic changes by using fluorescence lifetimes to quantify distance distributions between a donor fluorophore and a metal ion acceptor.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the tmFRET technique.

claim: The tmFRET method is applicable to both soluble and membrane protein structures under physiological conditions.
source: Importantly, our tmFRET method is applicable to both soluble and membrane protein structures under physiological conditions, making it ideal for studying SthK dynamics and membrane proteins more broadly.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the tmFRET method.

claim: TCSPC provides several advantages over frequency-domain measurements on a fluorescence lifetime imaging microscope (FLIM).
source: We believe that TCSPC provides several advantages over our previously utilized frequency-domain measurements on a fluorescence lifetime imaging microscope (FLIM).
evidence: This is an assertion about the comparative advantages of TCSPC.

claim: The TCSPC cuvette-based instrument allowed use of ~10 fold lower protein concentrations than required for previous experiments.
source: The TCSPC cuvette-based instrument has a longer path length than an imaging microscope and, therefore, allowed us to use ~10 fold lower protein concentrations.
evidence: This describes a practical advantage of the TCSPC method.

claim: The noise in TCSPC data is due to single-photon shot noise and can be well described by a Poisson distribution (above 10 photons).
source: Additionally, unlike frequency domain measurements, the noise in TCSPC data is due to single-photon shot noise and thus can be well described by a Poisson distribution (above 10 photons), making the χ2 determinations of model fits more meaningful (Lakowicz, 2006).
evidence: This describes a statistical advantage of TCSPC, supported by a citation.

claim: TCSPC allows for better accounting of background fluorescence by direct measurement.
source: Lastly, TCSPC allows for better accounting of the background fluorescence by direct measurement, which allows for more reliably fitting of data regardless of protein concentration or buffer conditions.
evidence: This describes another advantage of the TCSPC method.

claim: Lifetimes measured with TCSPC decrease in the presence of FRET.
source: As in the frequency domain experiments, lifetimes measured with TCSPC decrease in the presence of FRET.
evidence: This describes the expected behavior of FRET measurements.

claim: TCSPC data can be fit by a model with a distribution of distances that describes the measured FRET between donor and acceptor molecules.
source: These data can be fit by a model with a distribution of distances that describes the measured FRET between donor and acceptor molecules in the sample.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach used.

claim: The distance distribution accounts for heterogeneity within and between conformational states of the protein.
source: This distance distribution accounts for heterogeneity within and between conformational states of the protein, the latter of which is directly related to the energetics of conformational transitions through the Boltzmann relationship (Eggan et al., 2024; Lakowicz, 2006).
evidence: This describes how the distance distribution relates to protein energetics, supported by citations.

claim: SthKCterm was expressed with the noncanonical amino acid Acd at S361 and a cysteine at V416 for metal-ion acceptor conjugation.
source: In these experiments, SthKCterm, comprised of the isolated C-linker domain and CNBD, was expressed with the noncanonical amino acid acridon-2-ylalanine, Acd, at S361 and a cysteine at V416 for metal-ion acceptor conjugation.
evidence: This describes the experimental construct used.

claim: SthKCterm incorporating Acd was purified and mixed with excess WT unlabeled SthKCterm to create heterotetrameric protein.
source: As previously described, SthKCterm incorporating Acd was purified and mixed with excess WT unlabeled SthKCterm, to create heterotetrameric SthKCterm:WT/S361Acd-V416C protein (cartoon in Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the protein preparation method.

claim: The heteromeric channel eliminated the possibility of FRET between neighboring subunits.
source: This heteromeric channel eliminated the possibility of FRET between neighboring subunits (Eggan et al., 2024).
evidence: This describes the rationale for using heteromeric channels, supported by a citation.

claim: The donor-only SthKCterm:S361Acd protein lifetime was best fit with a double exponential decay, with 87% of the amplitude arising from a 17.6 ns lifetime and the remaining contribution from a second 4.73 ns lifetime.
source: We observed that this lifetime, while approximating a single-exponential decay, was best fit with a double exponential decay, with 87% of the amplitude arising from a 17.6 ns lifetime and the remaining contribution from a second 4.73 ns lifetime.
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data.

claim: The SthKCterm:S361Acd donor-only protein lifetime did not significantly change in the presence of cAMP.
source: The SthKCterm:S361Acd donor-only protein lifetime did not significantly change in the presence of cAMP, as expected (orange trace, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with expectations.

claim: Labeling SthKCterm:WT/S361Acd-V416C with [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ decreased the overall lifetime of Acd compared to the donor-only lifetime because of FRET.
source: As expected, labeling this construct with [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ decreased the overall lifetime of Acd compared to the donor-only lifetime because of FRET.
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with FRET.

claim: Upon addition of 1 µM cAMP, the lifetime of Acd decreased, and upon addition of 320 µM cAMP decreased yet further.
source: Subsequently, upon the addition of a subsaturating concentration of 1 µM cAMP, the lifetime of Acd decreased (blue trace, Figure 2B), and upon addition of a saturating concentration of 320 µM cAMP decreased yet further (red trace, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from TCSPC measurements.

claim: The decrease in fluorescence lifetime indicates increased FRET and shorter distances between the donor and acceptor molecules in response to cAMP.
source: This decrease in the fluorescence lifetime indicates increased FRET and shorter distances between the donor and acceptor molecules in response to cAMP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data based on FRET principles.

claim: The TCSPC approach has the sensitivity to measure ligand-triggered conformational changes in the CNBD of SthKCterm.
source: Overall, these cAMP-induced decreases in lifetimes, compared with our control without acceptor, demonstrate that our TCSPC approach has the sensitivity to measure ligand-triggered conformational changes in the CNBD of SthKCterm.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The two Gaussians represent the resting and active conformational states of the CNBD C-helix.
source: These two Gaussians represent the resting and active conformational states of the CNBD C-helix.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model parameters.

claim: The fits converged with a reduced χ2 near 1, and the parameters were well-identified.
source: These fits converged with a reduced χ2 near 1, and the parameters were well-identified (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the quality of the fits to the data.

claim: These distance values were similar to previously published frequency domain results of the same donor-acceptor.
source: These values were similar to our previously published frequency domain results of this same donor-acceptor, however, the σ values showed less state dependence (Figure 2C; Eggan et al., 2024).
evidence: This compares current results to previous work.

claim: The computationally predicted distance distributions show a remarkable similarity to those based on fits to experimental data.
source: These computationally predicted distance distributions show a remarkable similarity to those based on fits to our experimental data.
evidence: This compares computational predictions to experimental results.

claim: This KD value is comparable to the value obtained previously using steady-state tmFRET.
source: This KD value is comparable to the value obtained previously using steady-state tmFRET (Eggan et al., 2024).
evidence: This compares current results to previous work.

claim: TCSPC determined distance distributions at least as well as the previous frequency domain approach.
source: Based on these data, TCSPC determined distance distributions at least as well as our previous frequency domain approach.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing TCSPC and frequency domain results.

claim: Shorter lifetimes were measured in heterotetramers with a single donor and three acceptors than observed for control donor-only protein, both in the absence and presence of cAMP.
source: We measured shorter lifetimes in these heterotetramers than observed for control donor-only protein, both in the absence and presence of cAMP (Figure 3B, black and red traces, respectively).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from TCSPC measurements.

claim: The resting and active distributions aligned well with the intersubunit distance distributions predicted by chiLife.
source: The resting and active distributions aligned well with the intersubunit distance distributions predicted by chiLife (Figure 3D).
evidence: This compares experimental results to computational predictions.

claim: The fits most closely aligned with the shortest predicted intersubunit distance, conforming to expectations that the closest distances would dominate the FRET.
source: Indeed, the fits most closely aligned with the shortest predicted intersubunit distance, conforming to expectations that the closest distances would dominate the FRET.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results based on FRET principles.

claim: Intersubunit FRET must be considered when fitting data from experiments with homotetrameric SthK with all four subunits labeled with donor and acceptor.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that intersubunit FRET must be considered when fitting data from experiments with homotetrameric SthK with all four subunits labeled with donor and acceptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the intersubunit FRET measurements.

claim: There are only minimal differences in the distribution among resting and active states between the homotetrameric and heterotetrameric protein.
source: Based on these data, we conclude that there are only minimal differences in the distribution among resting and active states between the homotetrameric and heterotetrameric protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the two protein constructs.

claim: SthKFull was successfully purified as confirmed with in-gel fluorescence.
source: SthKFull:S361Acd-V416C (with cysteine) and SthKFull:S361Acd (without cysteine) were successfully purified as confirmed with in-gel fluorescence (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an experimental result confirmed by gel analysis.

claim: Coomassie staining showed a small proportion of protein subunits (<15%) that appeared truncated at the TAG codon site and copurified with full-length subunits.
source: Coomassie staining showed a small proportion of protein subunits (<15%) that appeared truncated at the TAG codon site and copurified with full-length subunits.
evidence: This is an observation from gel analysis.

claim: Size exclusion chromatography showed predominantly a single peak in Acd fluorescence without aggregates, indicating monodispersed well-behaved protein.
source: Size exclusion chromatography showed predominantly a single peak in Acd fluorescence without aggregates, indicating monodispersed well-behaved protein (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an experimental result from chromatography.

claim: The lifetime of SthKFull:S361Acd donor-only protein was similar to that of SthKCterm:S361Acd.
source: The lifetime of SthKFull:S361Acd donor-only protein was similar to that of SthKCterm:S361Acd (Figure 6B, gray trace), and the addition of cAMP did not change the lifetime (Figure 6B, orange trace).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from TCSPC measurements.

claim: The lifetime of SthKFull:S361Acd-V416C became shorter upon labeling with [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+.
source: As expected, the lifetime of SthKFull:S361Acd-V416C became shorter upon labeling with [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ (Figure 6B, black).
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with FRET.

claim: The addition of a range of cAMP concentrations to SthKFull:S361Acd-V416C-[Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ protein further decreased the lifetimes.
source: The addition of a range of cAMP concentrations (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, and 320 µM) to SthKFull:S361Acd-V416C-[Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ protein further decreased the lifetimes, following the same trend as was observed in the SthKCterm protein (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from TCSPC measurements.

claim: The dose-response relationship for SthKFull was fit with a quadratic equation to give a KD = 0.52 µM.
source: This relationship was fit with a quadratic equation to give a KD = 0.52 µM, which is comparable to that obtained from the SthKCterm but substantially lower than the KD reported from WT-SthK electrophysiology experiments (KD = 1.5 µM) (Morgan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a result from fitting dose-response data, compared to literature values.

claim: In the SthKCterm protein construct, the resting to active conformational transition is unfavorable in the absence of ligand (ΔG = +1.15 kcal/mol) and is more favorable in the presence of saturating cAMP (ΔG=–1.87 kcal/mol).
source: In the SthKCterm protein construct, the resting to active conformational transition is unfavorable in the absence of ligand (ΔG = +1.15 kcal/mol) and is more favorable in the presence of saturating cAMP (ΔG=–1.87 kcal/mol).
evidence: These are calculated energetics based on the experimental data.

claim: In SthKFull with attached pore and transmembrane domains, the resting to active transition without ligand is still unfavorable (ΔG = +0.22 kcal/mol), but more favorable than in SthKCterm, and cAMP further stabilizes the transition (ΔG=–2.87 kcal/mol).
source: In comparison, in SthKFull with attached pore and transmembrane domains, the resting to active transition without ligand is still unfavorable (ΔG = +0.22 kcal/mol), but more favorable than in SthKCterm, and cAMP further stabilizes the transition (ΔG=–2.87 kcal/mol).
evidence: These are calculated energetics based on the experimental data.

claim: Coupling between the pore and the cytoplasmic domain stabilizes the active state of the CNBD by about –1 kcal/mol.
source: This suggests coupling between the pore and the cytoplasmic domain stabilizes the active state of the CNBD by about –1 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the energetics of SthKFull and SthKCterm.

claim: ΔΔG for SthKCterm (–3.03 kcal/mol) and SthKFull (–3.10 kcal/mol) were very similar.
source: Interestingly, ΔΔG for SthKCterm (–3.03 kcal/mol) and SthKFull (–3.10 kcal/mol) were very similar.
evidence: This is a comparison of calculated energetics from the experimental data.

claim: The donor-acceptor distances were remarkably consistent across all constructs, within ~1.5 Å, both in the absence of cAMP and in the presence of a saturating concentration of cAMP.
source: We found that the donor-acceptor distances were remarkably consistent across all constructs, within ~1.5 Å, both in the absence of cAMP and in the presence of a saturating concentration of cAMP.
evidence: This is a summary of the distance measurements across different constructs.

claim: The stabilization of the active state relative to the resting state in the full-length channel was observed in both the absence of cAMP and in the presence of a saturating concentration of cAMP.
source: This stabilization of the active state relative to the resting state in the full-length channel was observed in both the absence of cAMP and in the presence of a saturating concentration of cAMP, i.e., it was not cAMP-dependent.
evidence: This is a key finding about the nature of the coupling.

claim: The difference in ΔG values between the no ligand and fully-liganded conditions (ΔΔG) was the same for both the C-terminal fragment and full-length channels.
source: Consequently, the difference in ΔG values between the no ligand and fully-liganded conditions (ΔΔG) was the same for both the C-terminal fragment and full-length channels.
evidence: This is a key finding about the energetics of ligand binding.

claim: The small but significant intersubunit FRET observed required consideration of this contribution in the FRET model.
source: The small but significant intersubunit FRET we observed required that we consider this contribution in our FRET model with which we fit our lifetime data.
evidence: This describes a methodological consideration based on experimental observations.

claim: All fits to the data converged and gave χ2 values near 1.
source: Although all fits to the data converged and gave χ2 values near 1, representing intersubunit donor-acceptor distances as arising from a single additional acceptor may not fully capture the intersubunit distance distribution in a tetrameric protein.
evidence: This describes the quality of the fits and a limitation of the model.

claim: The data showing more favorable activation of the CNBD in the full-length channel are consistent with a model in which the resting CNBD works on the pore to close it.
source: Our data, showing more favorable activation of the CNBD in the full-length channel containing the pore, are consistent with the second model in which the resting CNBD works on the pore to close it.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results in the context of allosteric models.

claim: A similar conclusion was reached for HCN1 channels and spHCN channels, for which deleting the C-terminal domains gave more favorable activation of the pore in electrophysiology experiments.
source: A similar conclusion was reached for HCN1 channels and spHCN channels, for which deleting the C-terminal domains gave more favorable activation of the pore in electrophysiology experiments (Vemana et al., 2004; Flynn and Zagotta, 2011; Wainger et al., 2001).
evidence: This compares the current findings to previous work on related channels, supported by citations.

claim: The conclusions from the present study are limited because the FRET reporters were only in the CNBD and came from a single donor-acceptor pair.
source: Our conclusions from the present study are limited because our FRET reporters were only in the CNBD and came from a single donor-acceptor pair, with further advances requiring FRET reporters in the C-linker and pore.
evidence: This acknowledges limitations of the current study.

claim: The study did not observe cooperativity between subunits for the CNBD conformational change.
source: Additionally, we did not observe cooperativity between subunits for the CNBD conformational change, and future experiments should investigate where intersubunit cooperativity might arise in these channels.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data and a suggestion for future work.
